item.description: Dingle manager Padraig Corcoran said there was no better man than Conor Geaney to kick the game winning score in the AIB Munster Senior Club Football Championship final. Geaney's two pointer in added on time saw them edges past St.Finbarrs by 1-18 to 20 points to become provincial champions for the first time. item.title: Duo expected to make Leinster return this week
item.description: Both James Lowe and Will Connors are expected to make a return for Leinster ahead of their Champions Cup clash with Leicester Tigers this Friday. Lowe is available for selection again after recovering from injury while Will Connors will be evaluated as the week goes on. Meanwhile, RG Snyman and Garry Ringrose will be further assessed after being withdrawn from last Saturday's win over the Harlequins. Advertisement

item.title: Salah left out of Liverpool squad
item.description: Mohamed Salah has been left out of Liverpool's squad ahead of their trip to Inter Milan in the Champions League tomorrow. His exclusion from the team is a club decision and has been backed by head coach Arne Slot. The decision comes following comments made by the Egyptian international after Liverpool's 3-all draw with Leeds last Saturday. item.title: Trial adjourned of former soldier accused of murder of Mid Kerry pensioner
item.description: The trial of a former soldier accused of murdering a mid Kerry pensioner has been adjourned. Thomas Carroll, with an address at Brookway, Clonmel, Co Tipperary, is before Mr Justice Patrick McGrath at Limerick Central Criminal Court. The 67-year-old is accused of murdering 84-year-old Patrick 'Paddy' O’Mahony in February 2024 at Ballyreameen, near Castlemaine. item.title: Farm hazardous waste collection in Listowel postponed due to weather
item.description: A farm hazardous waste collection day in Listowel tomorrow has been postponed due to the weather. The collection day was due to take place tomorrow at Listowel Mart. The Department of Agriculture has confirmed the hazardous waste collection day has been postponed, and rescheduled for next week, Tuesday 16th December, 9am to 4pm. item.title: Kerry County Council, Gardaí and emergency services met this afternoon as Storm Bran approaches
item.description: Kerry County Council is appealing to people to stay away from exposed coasts tomorrow, as Storm Bram is set to reach Kerry at 7am. Met Éireann has issued an orange wind warning for Kerry, effective from 7am to 3pm tomorrow. A yellow rain warning will be in place beforehand from nine o’clock tonight to nine tomorrow morning.
